original_run.timing_limitations: Nonverbose log has no per-statement or per-goroutine timestamps, CPU profile, fsync duration, deadline-entry timestamp or contemporaneous pressure counters. Leaf durations include fixture construction and cleanup. Parent parallel-test elapsed times exclude time waiting for parallel children and are not additive.

conclusion.summary: One failure is a preliminary raw WAL read, two are operation-guard unconfirmed-commit outcomes at an existing fixed deadline, and one is an invalid whole-API one-second oracle. Concurrent disk-backed fixtures and scheduling/I/O pressure are credible contributors, but the original run did not measure them. Preserve all product deadlines and safety assertions; isolate deadline-sensitive tests before attributing failures to production.
conclusion.no_production_change_recommended: Keep operationContext(0), immediateWorkBudget=1s, zero writer-lock wait, current commit uncertainty classification and no automatic retry. A timeout after COMMIT starts must not be recast as ErrStoreBusy/no-write.

contract_and_code.finding: Status first reads the live row, checks the exact process identity and reads the runtime binding. Only then does MarkCursorMissingIfSameLaunch start the terminal transaction. ReadLiveCursorSpawn and ReadCursorRuntime are ordinary s.db.QueryRow calls. The documented one-second allowance explicitly excludes preceding reads/process probes and multiple List candidates. No whole public API one-second deadline exists.

terminalMarkWithoutWait creates one operationContext(0), shares it through transaction/cleanup/audit, and never renews it. Zero wait means a 1ms pool-acquisition allowance, busy timeout zero and immediate SQLITE_BUSY on independently held writer contention. immediateWorkBudget is one second of execution allowance, not a one-second lock retry.

operation_guard is returned when the absolute operation deadline fires after commitStarted was set and before a completed result was published. This proves the guarded operation reached the COMMIT phase, not that COMMIT failed or rolled back. ErrStoreBusy is appropriate before COMMIT; uncertainty afterward is deliberately distinct. The branch alone does not measure time spent in fsync versus Go scheduling or driver/native work.

concurrency_and_resource_evidence.supported_inference: Default Go test parallelism plus hundreds of real-store fixture sites can create CPU and storage contention. The 250ms first-read expiry and two one-second COMMIT-phase expiries are compatible with that mechanism. Original data cannot attribute the cause exclusively to load or establish an exact concurrency count.
